speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are aware that this is a hot topic on the ground.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We hear it from our residents; we hear it from many Members of this House.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: All have expressed concern over the irresponsible use of PMDs, which have caused a lot of trouble.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Reckless PMD riders have become a menace on the ground, causing alarm on our public paths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: People are worried about whether our elderly parents or young children will be able to avoid speeding PMD users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Speedsters have also illegally modified their devices to travel at very high speed, without fear for their own lives and the danger they put others in.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Residents are also worried that their houses would be affected should their neighbour’s PMD catch fire.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Such irresponsible behaviour is unacceptable and cannot be tolerated.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, we are mindful that tens of thousands of Singaporeans have adopted PMDs and benefited daily from their usage.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The vast majority of them use PMDs responsibly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Through the course of my various engagements, fellow Singaporeans have related to me stories of Singaporeans who have saved time and costs by using PMDs as a transport option, older Singaporeans with mobility challenges who have found newfound freedom with personal mobility aids, and Singaporeans who have improved their livelihoods through new employment opportunities.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Low used to get around on a bicycle.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But with age, this has become a bit more challenging for him.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Two years ago, Mr Low started riding an e-scooter, which he finds is a convenient way to travel.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: He uses his e-scooter to run errands near his home in Sengkang, do weekend patrols with the Waterways Watch Society where he volunteers, and even visit his brother in Bedok.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For Mr Low, his e-scooter helps him stay active and connected and has since become a way of life for him.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are also thousands of Singaporeans who use PMDs to improve their livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: He had to give up his earlier job due to health reasons and doing food delivery is now his lifeline.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As the eldest son in his family, working as a food delivery PMD rider allows Mr Hafidz to provide for himself and his elderly parents, who are no longer working.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: When I met him last week at a dialogue session, he shared with me that his goal is simply to ride safely with his loved ones in mind.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Mr Low and Mr Hafidz are only two of the many Singaporeans who have benefited from the introduction of PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Even Singaporeans who do not ride PMDs benefit from the convenient services provided by riders who use PMDs to deliver food to their doorsteps.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Because we were aware of the potential negative effects and also benefits, we conducted an extensive public consultation exercise to solicit views from a wide range of key stakeholders back in 2015 and 2016.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It was led by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim and his Active Mobility Advisory Panel (AMAP).

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Members of the House will remember our thorough debate on all these issues when the Active Mobility Bill was tabled in January 2017.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: On balance, the House decided to allow PMDs to enter Singapore as they are fundamentally a cheap, convenient and environmentally friendly alternative to cars and motorcycles for short trips.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They can play an important role in our vision for a car-lite society.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Members wisely emphasised the need for regulations, enforcement, public education and, wherever suitable, infrastructure enhancement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The growing number of fires is, indeed, worrying.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I have often asked myself whether we would be better off banning PMDs whenever I read of accidents involving PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, I remember the call to ban bicycles from footpaths several years ago.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: After intensive public education efforts and infrastructure improvements, there is now a greater acceptance of bicycles in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is the rider who decides whether it is beneficial or detrimental to lives.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am confident that Singaporeans can be taught to use PMDs responsibly, as they have with bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am confident that we can bring about the safe sharing of paths with PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But with the hindsight of experience, we should add new regulatory measures to enhance safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I will focus on two key areas – fire safety and path safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, how can we further enhance fire safety?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The UL2272 standard improves safety against fire and electrical hazards significantly, by requiring the devices to pass a stringent set of tests conducted by accredited testing centres under extreme physical conditions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We could have simply banned non-UL2272 certified PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But retailers and users who had just bought such PMDs pleaded for some grace period.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: That is why we imposed the requirement for PMD retailers to sell only UL2272-certified devices from 1 July 2019, while users could only ride certified devices from 1 January 2021 onwards.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Even with this grace period, many retailers complained bitterly about the adverse impact on their businesses.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Users were also unhappy about having to give up devices that were still usable and having to pay significantly more for a UL2272-certified PMD.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These negative sentiments were widely covered in the media.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As many Singaporeans rely on PMDs for their livelihoods and their commuting needs, we think this is the earliest reasonable deadline.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will be scheduling all e-scooters which were earlier registered and self-declared UL2272-certified for inspection.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Some PMD users are concerned about the costs of switching out their non UL2272-certified devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While I understand their worries, we seek their understanding and support for this necessary move.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: AMAP Chairman Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim and I recently met with food delivery riders to see how they will be impacted by these proposed new measures and how we can help cushion the impact on them.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The food delivery companies have tied up with PMD operators to offer PMD rentals for food delivery riders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They have also announced their commitment to help their riders convert to, or rent, UL2272-certified devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will work with food delivery companies to offer more attractive rates for PMD rentals.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: From LTA’s engagement with retailers, we are also aware that they will bring in more UL2272-certified PMDs with higher capacity and longer range very soon.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I strongly encourage and urge all users and owners of the non UL2272-certified PMDs to switch them out as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They can be a fire risk if you still keep and charge them at home.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These devices should be properly and safely disposed of as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will provide support to PMD users who come forth to dispose of their non UL2272-certified PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are studying ways to encourage Singaporeans to come forth and dispose of their non UL2272-certified devices early.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is also working with NEA to ensure safe and convenient disposal of non UL2272-certified devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I wish to remind PMD users that UL2272-certified PMDs come with electrical system safety features to reduce the risk of fires.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: UL2272 automatically cuts off battery charging once the battery is fully charged, thus avoiding overcharging which is a cause of fire.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For this reason, modifying the electrical system of a UL2272-certified device will invalidate the certification.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Users should not try to modify devices which are already UL2272-certified or add battery packs, as this could affect the circuitry and device safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Device owners should instead approach their retailer or an authorised agent who is familiar with the approved battery model for that device model for battery replacements, so as not to void the UL2272 certification.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While UL2272 is a rigorous standard, users still have a part to play by adopting safe charging practices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They should avoid charging already-full batteries and regularly check batteries for damage or deformity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They should only use original power adaptors, which should be affixed with Enterprise Singapore’s Safety Mark.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Users should never leave their devices unattended when charging.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In particular, devices should not be left to charge overnight.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will work with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) to strengthen educational campaigns and outreach programmes on UL2272 certification and safe charging practices for residential, industrial and commercial buildings.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will also crack down on illegal modifications of PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Individuals caught doing so will be liable for a fine and/or jail term.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Our strategy covers infrastructure enhancement, enforcement and education.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We expect the number to grow as more Singaporeans take up the opportunities afforded by this new mobility option.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will work with local Members of Parliament (MPs) and residents to identify the infrastructure improvements to tackle specific hotspots in each of your constituency.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Two months ago, we had a discussion in this House on whether PMDs should be banned from HDB void decks and corridors, where there are many blind spots which cannot be overcome through infrastructure improvements.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At that time, I said that Town Councils could set and enforce their own rules on PMD usage at void decks.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition, some Town Councils have also told us about the high accident risk at crowded town centres and neighbourhood centres where the paths are lined with shops.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As pedestrians can walk in all different directions, there is a potentially higher risk of accidents, compared to a linear footpath.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, we are actually selecting five trial sites.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will consult the local MP on the specific details.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If the concept of the POZ proves useful, we will roll it out to other towns island-wide.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As a further step, LTA has also started a trial to implement School Zone markings along footpaths outside some schools.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These include speed regulating strips, “SLOW” markings and enhanced visual cues on the ground to remind PMD users to slow down and watch out for other path users, especially young children.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have completed works at the first trial site at Fern Green Primary School.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will expand this to four other schools which include Fengshan Primary, Jiemin Primary, Rivervale Primary and Yishun Secondary School by next month.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Apart from localised infrastructure enhancements, we work closely with the local MP to develop active mobility infrastructure at the township level.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Ang Mo Kio (AMK) is an example of what every town can look forward to.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: AMK is our first “Walking and Cycling Town”.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: When the cycling-path network is completed in 2022, it will span 20 kilometres (km), connecting homes safely and seamlessly to the Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) station, bus interchange and AMK Hub.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These cycling paths will be located along almost all of the main roads in AMK.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They will have pedestrian and cyclist friendly features, such as pedestrian-priority zones near bus stops, a distinctive red colouring for the cycling paths, and cycling ramps.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are four stretches where it is necessary to build cycling paths for connectivity, but where the sidewalks are not wide enough.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These four stretches are at AMK Streets 22, 41, 43 and 61.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To ensure a safe and well-connected network of cycling paths, we will reclaim road space to build the cycling paths at these four stretches.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will be done by reducing the width of roads or taking back an entire road lane.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The works at AMK will be completed over the next three years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will progressively implement similar plans in other HDB towns, and I seek Members' and fellow Singaporeans’ patience and support.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the national level, there are now 440 km of cycling paths in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will require us to reclaim some existing car lanes.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In new precincts, such as Kampong Bugis, Tengah and Woodlands North Coast, LTA plans to build cycling paths on both sides of the road.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: New cycling paths may also be added to private residential estates and industrial estates.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also need to have a comprehensive enforcement and education strategy to encourage responsible riding and deter errant riding.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has significantly stepped up enforcement against errant riders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will be supplemented by crowdsource feedback through LTA's recently-launched "Report PMD/power-assisted bicycles (PAB) Incident" function in the MyTransport.SG app.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Since May 2018, LTA officers have detected over 4,900 active mobility offences and impounded over 2,100 non-compliant devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are, therefore, leveraging technology to expand our enforcement reach.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has just started on an 18-month trial of mobile closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at hotspot locations to determine the effectiveness of video analytics software and radar technology in detecting offences, such as speeding.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We take a tough stance against retailers who display or sell non-compliant devices, as well as those who provide illegal device modification services.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To date, LTA has taken action against 12 PMD retailers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is essential to tackle non-compliant devices at the source.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will not tolerate such behaviour and we will deal with them firmly and with the full brunt of the law.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Some Members also asked whether our penalties are adequate.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The laws allow for a range of penalties, ranging from composition sums, forfeiture of non-compliant devices, to fine and jail terms for serious cases.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This ensures that the punishment is proportionate to the crime.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In February 2019, the Courts ruled in a landmark case, sentencing a reckless PMD rider to seven weeks' jail for knocking down a pedestrian and causing grievous hurt.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will serve as a precedent for future cases.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are closely monitoring whether our penalty regime is effective at deterring errant riding behaviour.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I have also asked Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim and AMAP to study the issue of insurance and compensation in the event of active mobility-related incidents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: AMAP and LTA are also working together with insurance companies to come up with more affordable products for individuals and encouraging individuals to purchase insurance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has brought the Safe Riding Programme (SRP) to local communities and schools, with about 600 sessions conducted over the last three months alone.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Such educational efforts are key to a fundamental shift in how all path users behave and will help us to maximise the usage of our paths in a safe manner.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As our population ages, it is important to promote active ageing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Regular exercise is an important part of active ageing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is why we promote Walk, Cycle, Ride as a preferred mode of transport for short distances within our residential estates.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For some Singaporeans, motorised PMDs offer an added option.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We hope Singaporeans will be able to accept their usage on our footpaths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But this requires PMD users to behave themselves.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is for their own safety as well as the safety of others.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have had a year of experience regulating PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It has not been all smooth sailing and we did not expect any new tool’s introduction to be a rosy journey.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But the experience has helped us to review our regulatory measures and to see how they can be tightened to further enhance safety.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As with any new technology, our regulatory regime has to be nimble and responsive.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will get the new measures in place quickly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And we will continue to monitor their effectiveness.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And we remain ready to introduce new or better measures, if necessary.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And we will not fail Singaporeans in safeguarding their lives and welfare.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Singapore is actually not alone in having to grapple with PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am also grateful to AMAP for their wise counsel and unceasing efforts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Above all, I seek Singaporeans' support and understanding that we are committed to doing our utmost.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am confident that we will be able to make active mobility safe and relevant for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned about the new deadlines of April and July 2020.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Whilst this is a welcomed move, it is still eight to 11 months away.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Given the high numbers of fires involving PMDs recently, is there anything else that MOT can do to mitigate these things that are happening?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We understand that many Singaporeans rely on PMDs for their livelihoods and their commuting needs, such as the stories of Mr Hafidz and Mr Low that I have shared.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And we understand that if we were to ban non UL2272-certified devices immediately, that would definitely impose a lot of hardship and inconvenience to many Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, in the meantime, what we can do is that we will continue to encourage non UL2272-certified device owners to switch to compliant ones as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Just to remind Members of the House as well as all Singaporeans, we can actually minimise the risk of fire by avoiding overcharging the batteries, like I mentioned before.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We should avoid illegally modifying the devices and also avoid tampering with the electrical components or leaving the devices unattended when charging.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If possible, please do not leave your PMD to charge overnight because there is a tendency for the device to overheat if you overcharge it excessively beyond what is required.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Owners should also check that the batteries are in good condition, look for any damages or deformities that may give an indication that the battery may not be safe to continue to be used.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And we should also make sure that original power adapters affixed with the Enterprise Singapore Safety Mark are used to charge the devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, these are some of the practical advice I would give Singaporeans while we await the implementation of the new deadline.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Every time I have a dialogue, I get an earful from my residents saying how dangerous it is to walk on these footpaths because the PMDs just come up behind them silently.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, with these measures, is MOT or LTA simply being reactive rather than trying to pre-empt the problem?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I understand some countries have already banned PMDs from footpaths.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Has LTA considered banning these PMDs from footpaths until our infrastructure is improved?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Last month, I filed a Parliamentary Question about park connectors and asked why the National Parks Board (NParks) are not prepared to draw lines demarcating areas for pedestrians from those for PMDs.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But NParks said no, they are not prepared to do so.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And that adds to the complication because pedestrians do not know for sure.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If I run left, I get knocked; I run right, I also get knocked down.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, really, this situation is quite urgent and safety should be paramount.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Would MOT really consider banning PMDs until our infrastructure is improved?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If they just get fined, they make it all back from selling such non-compliant batteries and PMDs.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Let us give them a heftier punishment, even send them to jail if necessary, so that everyone will know the importance of compliance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, we had various discussions on these issues on PMD safety over the past one to two years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And MOT really appreciates all the feedback given by Members of the House.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And if we look at some of these measures that we have come up with, it shows that we are listening, we know the concerns on the ground and we will not hesitate to take necessary action whenever appropriate.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But I would also like to remind all Members that the reason why we promote active mobility is because we believe that it is good for Singaporeans and Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And that it helps with our vision of a car-lite society.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As with the introduction of any new technology, our regulatory regime has to be nimble and responsive, like I mentioned in my Ministerial Statement, and that we will have to evolve with the needs according to the situation and feedback on the ground.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Member has also rightly pointed out that we could have banned PMD use right from the beginning or even at this point in time until all the infrastructure is ready.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We could have taken the path of least resistance at the beginning to completely ban PMDs on pavements and shared paths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But I think we debated in the House during the introduction of the Active Mobility Bill that, taking all things into consideration, PMDs still have a role to play in providing active mobility options as well as providing first- and last-mile connectivity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And if we had banned PMD use on pathways, what it actually means is that we would have just pushed PMDs onto the roads, which would likely lead to more fatalities because of the higher speed of buses, cars and lorries travelling on the same road.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Instead, what we have done is to implement a very comprehensive regime to ensure that PMDs are used in a safe and responsible manner.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With that, I want to urge Singaporeans to continue to work with us in making active mobility a safe and relevant option for everyone.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the Member's questions on enforcement on some of these errant retailers who are irresponsibly selling devices that are non-compliant, LTA will definitely take a very close watch and will not hesitate to take tough actions against them.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Also, with regard to the question on the Park Connector Network (PCN) shared paths, currently, we are working with all the relevant agencies to see how we can enhance safety of PMD use on shared paths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will also be working with local advisers to see how we can have infrastructure enhancement to tackle some of these issues on the ground.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: First, will the Ministry consider licensing PMDs so as to manage the growth of PMDs in Singapore and also to make it compulsory for the PMD riders to attend a safe riding course?

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: Second, can the Ministry also consider reducing the speed limit on the approved PMD paths, especially those shared paths with pedestrians?

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: And third, the Town Councils welcome the five trial sites which LTA has identified in terms of designating them as POZs.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: We hope that the study will help us to better understand the behaviour of PMDs in these town centres.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: The Town Councils have plans to ban PMDs at all common property unless it is approved by the Town Council or LTA.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, we have started the mandatory registration of PMDs, and we have only started that recently.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, I would urge everyone to give it some time for it to take effect.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, we also strongly encourage all riders to go through the Safe Riding Programme (SRP) which I have mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: To encourage the take up of SRP, we have made it completely free of charge.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is fully subsidised for the first two years till December 2019.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, if you know of anyone who has not gone for the course, please encourage them to do so while it is free of charge.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to also work with active mobility interest groups, schools, companies, especially food-delivery companies, to encourage all their cyclists and PMD riders to attend SRP.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So far, we have received some feedback similar to what Dr Teo Ho Pin has shared as to whether these could be reduced further.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I have asked Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim, together with his AMAP team, to look at some of these suggestions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Hopefully, they will be able to come back with some recommendations by the end of this year.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the five trial sites, I would like to thank Dr Teo Ho Pin for agreeing to coordinate the efforts of implementing the trials in the five selected Town Councils.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, initially, we wanted to hold this trial over six months.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And if it is proven to be effective, we will extend it to all the different towns island-wide where necessary.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: A few supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: First, we recognise the advantages that PMDs bring to society and they can create jobs as well.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: By and large, we have no problems with many of the users who use PMDs responsibly.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The problem, as we know, is always with a small group of PMD users and also retailers who flout the rules.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, my first supplementary question to the Senior Minister of State concerns individual users who flout the rules, who do not know how to use it and endanger the lives, whether they use it on the roads or on the pathways.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We know so many cases where there are injuries, near misses and it is very difficult, much as we like, in terms of enforcement, how do we report them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My residents have told me that even if they want to, they do not know how.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The users zoom past them and there is no time to take a photo and all that.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, while the rules are there, the rules are no good if it is not enforced.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, can we think of ways where we either step up enforcement through technology or through more people?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I am sure it is a small fraction of the number of people we have to do this enforcement compared to the number of users that are on the road.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: So, that is my first question: how can we step up enforcement against irresponsible users, regardless of whether they are using on the road or on the pathways, because we cannot fix them, as what Mr Lim Biow Chuan has asked for?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My second question is: I also echo the concern about retailers who are outrightly selling things which they should not.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: For them, I think stiffer action needs to be taken.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: There should not be any two ways about it, and we should be firm, we should be hard and should send the right message across to both retailers and irresponsible users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The first one is on the small group of irresponsible users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I totally agree with him that the majority of PMD users are responsible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: How can we then enhance our enforcement actions against this small group of people?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Having said that, we do not want to ban the use of PMD just because of this small group of irresponsible users, while affecting the rest who are responsible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will review and monitor the reports that are received from this application.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Whenever possible, we will take enforcement action against the errant rider.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, we also understand that sometimes it may be difficult to identify the irresponsible user just through a picture taken using the app.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And I believe, with more manpower, we will be able to do more.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, LTA has stepped up enforcement actions to the extent that, almost on a daily basis, you will see that LTA has been putting up postings on its Facebook about some of these errant riders being summoned and some of these non-compliant devices being impounded.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the Member's second clarification on errant retailers, yes, indeed, I share the same sentiment that we should really get tough on some of these irresponsible retailers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I mentioned in my previous reply, we will not hesitate to take very stiff actions against some of these errant retailers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First of all, I would like to thank the Senior Minister of State for including Khatib Centre as one of the five piloted sites for POZs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, Khatib Centre has been POZed long before, until the Active Mobility Act came into force.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State to work closely with the local Member of Parliament.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have a lot more POZs in Nee Soon South that I would like to work with MOT on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is not just in Khatib Centre, but covered linkways as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Just now, the Senior of State mentioned that there are 90,000 PMDs registered so far.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Out of the 90,000, how many are non-compliant?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: From now until July, that is 11 months.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If the number is huge, a lot of us will have nightmares.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We would still have to worry about having to run in the middle of the night.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is: from 1 April, compulsory inspection before they can register their PMD.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is that a one-off inspection or will there be subsequent inspections?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because after that, they can do modifications as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The third question is that for those within 400 metres from MRT train stations, where you have covered linkways, those are the areas that normally we received a lot of feedback of near accidents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the infrastructure that he mentioned, the funding that he mentioned, will it be carried out for all the covered linkways within the 400 metres?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And I am glad to hear about using technology.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In fact, they shared with me that they have the technology, they can give us data on who is the top violator, at what time it passed by, at what speed it went by.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I hope that MOT can choose my area to be one of those piloted as well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First of all, let me just thank Er Dr Lee Bee Wah for supporting us in this effort.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, I must give credit to Er Dr Lee Bee Wah for the idea of POZs in town centres and neighbourhood centres.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I visited Khatib Town Centre together with Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and she showed me some of the challenges on the ground.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Through some of the feedback from Er Dr Lee as well as residents and other Town Council Chairmen and Advisors, we have, therefore, decided to implement and introduce these trials of POZs at the five selected town and neighbourhood centres.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But, of course, if it proves to be very useful and if we receive very good feedback from Advisors as well as residents, we will implement the POZs island-wide to other town areas which Advisors have identified as potential hotspots.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is necessary for the retailers to have sufficient time to bring in the certified devices for the replacement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This will allow us, first of all, to verify that, indeed, some of these so-called self-declared certified PMDs are really certified to the UL2272 standard.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Subsequently, what happens is that only PMDs that have been certified by our authorised inspection centres to be compliant will be allowed to be registered.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Whether this is going to be a one-off inspection or a periodic inspection, currently, we are discussing internally.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If Members understand the lifespan of a PMD, it is probably going to just last about two to three years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If we do have a regular inspection regime, whether that is going to be, first of all, necessary; secondly, whether it is going to be cost-effective.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Having said that, like I have shared, we are still discussing internally and, if necessary, we may put this as a requirement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will work with local Advisors to identify some of these hotspots and make the necessary infrastructural enhancements.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One relates to the issue of safe riding courses.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Government consider making it compulsory for all users of PMDs to attend safe riding courses?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned that, at the moment, there are about over 90,000 e-scooters that have been registered.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I wonder whether the Government has an estimation of how many e-scooters that have been imported and sold in Singapore that have not been registered so far.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We can just well imagine that the figure is definitely greater than 90,000.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And of all the e-scooters that have been used, surely, there are a lot of the e-scooters that have been used by more than one owner, that is, one scooter may be used by a few people in the family.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe that to create a culture of safe riding, it will also involve putting the public information on the rules and on the etiquette to the users, that is, to PMD users, as well as to other park users or path users, who may not actively seek out such information, so they may not go to the LTA Facebook, they may not access certain areas where PMD users may go and sign up for safe riding courses.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, a lot of elderly people may not access these Facebook sites and they are using the footpaths in our towns on an everyday basis.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How do we ensure, for example, the simple etiquette that has always been talked about, that we should keep left, whether it is a PMD user, bicycle or pedestrian?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How many persons actually consciously walk on a footpath or on a connector knowing that you keep left for safety —

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Maybe just allow me to answer the Member's Parliamentary Questions on PMD-sharing in private premises.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is to prevent indiscriminate parking of shared devices.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, the licensing regime currently does not cover PMD-sharing operators who deploy their devices solely on private land.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At present, PMDs belonging to commercial shared services operating from private land are allowed to travel on public paths so long as the rental does not end in a public place.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are watching this very closely, especially for PMD-sharing operators who flout this rule, and we will take action against them.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This even includes operators who offer PMD-sharing services from private premises.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Our licensing regime under the Parking Places Act requires PMD sharing licensees to procure as well as maintain third-party liability insurance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This does not apply to those operating solely on private land.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I hope this answers the two Parliamentary Questions that the Member had filed.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Member also asked about whether we have any information on the number of devices that are not registered so far.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As long as they are not registered, e-scooters cannot be used on public paths.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I encourage owners of such unregistered devices either to quickly register them or, if not, they should dispose of these devices in a safe and responsible manner.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to mandatory education on safe riding, we have also asked ourselves whether we should make it mandatory for all PMD users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But we concluded that at this point in time, it may not be necessary to do so.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to work with all the various interest groups to encourage people to take part in SRP.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have also published a Code of Conduct for PMD users and this was actually suggested by AMAP.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This provides PMD users with some guidelines on some of the things that they should do when riding a PMD responsibly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I also reckon that, sometimes, many of our elderly residents may not be aware of some of these rules and etiquette when using a public path.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Therefore, we have also engaged the community to help us in this public education effort, through the Active Mobility Patrol (AMP) teams that are currently present in more than 60 constituencies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I also want to encourage constituencies which do not have an AMP to please sign up for AMP.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA will work closely with Members to educate PMD users as well as your residents on the safe use of PMDs and pathways.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is the concern I had in the Parliamentary Question that I filed for answer in today's session.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The first is in relation to the spike in fire incidents.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: As the Members of the House may recall, Dr Lam Pin Min made an announcement in this House in September 2018 about the new standards.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Following that, retailers of PMDs dumped prices from $600 to about $200 to $300.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I believe this may have resulted in people buying these non-compliant PMDs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am not sure whether there is a correlation between this dumping and the higher incidents of fires involving PMDs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am also concerned whether or not these PMDs are fit for purpose.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Even though you charged the PMDs properly, they could still be fire hazards.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I wonder whether the Ministry could provide services to such PMD users to see whether their PMDs are fit for purpose.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The second question is in relation to the mandatory inspection date of 1 April 2020.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Given that only 10% of PMDs are compliant now and given that the amnesty ends on 1 July 2020, I would imagine that a good percentage of PMDs would fail the inspection, come 1 April 2020.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: What would be the status of such PMD users?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Perhaps we could consider providing value for scrapping such non-compliant PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, it is of great concern to LTA and MOT when we read of the statistics for PMD-related fires.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This can likely be attributed to the increase in the population of PMDs in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the 90% of the non-compliant PMDs, we will, like I have mentioned before, encourage owners to quickly change out to the UL2272-certified PMDs as soon as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If not, then we will want to remind PMD owners on some of the safe practices when it comes to the charging of the non UL2272-certified devices, which I had already elaborated on earlier.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Will there be a secondary market for non-compliant PMDs?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I hope not, as least not in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If we do find anyone using such non-compliant devices, they will be taken to task.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first is regarding the cost of the compulsory inspection.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would it be borne by the Government or the owners?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And would that be included in the fee for registration?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second one is whether there is a deregistration procedure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: After inspection, after, let us say, the battery's shelf life is gone and people are disposing of their PMDs, the PMDs might still be registered, but the PMDs are no longer in use.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Another scenario, the PMDs might still continue to be used but modified with the registration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, is there a deregistration process for PMDs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, regarding the UL2271 batteries, my understanding is that in some reports, there is some confusion with regard to UL2271 batteries that they can be used to replace batteries to make PMDs UL2272-compliant, like people buying UL2272 devices but then replacing the batteries with UL2271 batteries because they are of a higher quality, are more powerful and what not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is this allowed or would this make it non-compliant?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the cost of the inspection as well as the subsequent fee for registration when owners replace their PMDs, LTA is working out the details and will make the announcement soon.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to deregistration, there is currently a process for PMD users to deregister their registered PMDs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And I would want to remind owners to do so because failure to deregister will not take away your responsibility of being the owner of the PMD device if it is being used illegally subsequently.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, there is currently a deregistration process in place.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Please remember to deregister your PMD when you want to discard or stop using your PMD.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the last clarification on UL2271 and UL2272, I will have to check exactly whether they are compatible in terms of the certification.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: My understanding is that the device is certified to the UL2272 standard based on the battery and circuitry of the PMD.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But I need to verify if UL2271 is, indeed, a compatible one.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But I would encourage PMD users, if you need to change batteries, please go to a reputable retailer to have it changed.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Do not do it yourself or through some black market retailers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Go to reputable ones to ensure that the certification will not be rendered void.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: He actually mentioned that, if need be, a dedicated lane on the road would be set aside, if I heard him correctly.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State is whether the Government will consider, given the rising popularity of the use of PMDs and cycling, going back to the early years of Singapore where there was a dedicated cycling track on the road along with the vehicles but, obviously, doing it safely as part of the future LTA Transport Master Plan.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: When we mentioned dedicated lanes for cycling, it is separate from the road itself.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: From our feedback and experience, and looking at what some other countries have been doing, locating the dedicated cycling path next to the road has its pros and cons.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There is always the danger where the fast-moving vehicles on the road may pose a danger to the cyclist or PMD user.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: What we mentioned in AMK is that we will try to reclaim part of these roads so that we can make it as a footpath or dedicated cycling path, which is physically separated from the road itself.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is to ensure the safety of the slow-moving PMD users and the cyclists, as well as pedestrians.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I just have two other supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The first is whether we will consider mandating the licensing registration at the point of sale so that we are actually tackling both the retailers who have the onus or responsibility of sending the different products they are bringing in to Enterprise Singapore for that Safety Mark, but also to enable the users to know that what they are purchasing is of good quality or has already been certified.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Next, with regard to the use of technology, it is always possible with technology that we can mount gadgets on the PMD sets for sale since we are also asking the users to pay a licensing or registration fee.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The main thing is that, with technology, it can help to track the speed of the individual PMDs so that we do not have to triple or quadruple the number of enforcers on the ground.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The issue is very similar to that of high-rise littering or even pigeon-feeding.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: There can never be enough enforcers on the ground to help out with all this enforcement.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: With that technology, they can automatically trigger if there is any violation on the part of the PMD users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Whether we want to mandate registration at the point of sale is something that we can look at.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are not saying that we will disallow the registration by the retailer on behalf of the buyer.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But I would also like to remind users to purchase UL2272-certified or compliant PMDs from reputable retailers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: If you are going to buy PMDs online, then there is a risk that you may be purchasing something that has been falsely declared to be compliant but which actually may not be.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA is also embracing technology to see how we can enforce the responsible use of PMDs, such as, like I mentioned, the use of mobile CCTVs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Whenever there are new technologies that are available in the future, we will consider using such technology to enhance our enforcement action.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But in the interim, I think it is necessary to have sufficient manpower on the ground, which is one of the many pieces of feedback that we have received from Advisors that, in the past, there were very few physical bodies on the ground to do the enforcement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Therefore, we have increased the number of manpower to tackle the root of the problem.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But in the future, if we have technologies that can facilitate enforcement action, we will definitely deploy them.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Although several measures have since been implemented by the Ministry, I think we can all understand due to the sheer number of PMDs and the lack of sufficient enforcement resources on the ground, it is almost impossible and also impractical to police errant PMD users.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: When accidents happen, victims suffer, not only suffering the pain and inconvenience of injuries but having to foot large medical bills, not to mention the loss of earnings as well.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Without insurance, it is difficult for the victims to seek appropriate compensation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Taking the errant PMD user to Court may be fruitless, not to mention the high cost of litigation which the victim can ill afford.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A general search of the insurance market reveals that the premium for a basic third-party insurance policy, if made mandatory, may not be exorbitant.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: An indicative estimate may cost somewhere between $50 and $80 per annum, depending on the potential volume of PMDs that we have.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This would be an affordable price to pay to ensure proper and adequate compensation to victims of accidents involving PMDs as well as the fire risks from non-compliant devices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, given the large number of non-compliant PMDs still in use out there – and we still have many more months to go – I urge the Ministry to seriously reconsider the introduction of mandatory insurance in light of this real and imminent risk exposure.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, we had discussed this issue on several occasions in previous Parliamentary Sittings.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, this is one step in the correct direction.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, I hear your appeal and we will ask Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim to look into it.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Speaker, I have a clarification for the Senior Minister of State regarding retailers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I think earlier in his speech, he mentioned that action had been taken against a number of retailers for selling non-compliant devices.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I think the number was around 12, if I heard him correctly.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could the Senior Minister of State clarify whether any of these retailers were actually online retailers?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Related to that, I have come across a few people who have bought e-scooters from Taobao and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I wonder how the Government is going to work with these online retailers that are headquartered overseas where they may have an international market where being non-compliant with UL2272 is legal in those jurisdictions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But at this point in time, I do not have the exact information as to whether any of these are online retailers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like what Ms Sylvia Lim has rightly pointed out, we are cognisant of the fact that there are thousands of online shopping platforms out there, including Taobao, and many of them are actually based overseas outside Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will also continue to raise public awareness and educate both current as well as future users that it is illegal to use non-compliant devices on our public paths.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While I do not think that 81,000 PMDs will spontaneously catch fire, if it is a safety concern, why would LTA not call for an immediate ban on its usage?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In the car industry, even though it is just one or two accidents, Toyota has recalled 2.2 million cars before.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Ikea – furniture malfunction – has recalled the entire range.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For the food industry, even if it is not recalled internationally, when some food additives are found to be problematic, they are recalled in Singapore as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, if there is a safety concern, and we already see a significant number of fires that have resulted from improper usage or battery problems in the last two years, why do we not recall for that?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second supplementary question has to do with licensing of the rider or permitting the rider.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A couple of hon Members have already mentioned this.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Israel requires a special permit for riders who do not already have a driver’s licence.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: New Zealand also requires a driver’s licence, as in certain provinces in Canada.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, there are already jurisdictions that require licensing for riders.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While we may not have to go that far, my understanding from the Senior Minister of State’s response earlier is "not at this point".

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But at what point do we start considering it?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If we keep saying that it is not at this point and then two years down the road we will have to come back to the Parliament and have another Ministerial Statement on the issue.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, for the SRP, would it not be possible to make this compulsory?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And, for attendance of the course, you are granted, say, a letter or permit that would allow you to ride or purchase a PMD.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, non UL2272-certified devices have been identified as one of the possible reasons why we have this spate of fire incidents recently.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But we also understand that there are multiple factors that can lead to a fire incident.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As such, while we understand that there is a call to ban the use of non UL2272-certified devices immediately, we also are cognisant of the fact that there are many Singaporeans out there who rely on such devices, not only for their daily commuting, but also as a way to sustain their livelihood.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, we are quite careful in not doing that.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But at the same time, we want to remind PMD users who are currently not using UL2272-certified devices to exercise caution, like what I have mentioned about the safety practices, in terms of charging.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And if you are able to do that, then we will minimise the risks of fire incidents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But let us bring this back to study and see whether this will be necessary in the future.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have had a few PMD-related fire incidents in my ward over the past two years.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Since then, my residents have taken to charging their PMDs outside of their flats while attending to them.
